object.value: The G7 commit to develop proposals, with the OECD, GPAI and others, for monitoring tools and mechanisms to help organisations stay accountable for implementing the actions.

evidence.passage: We also commit to develop proposals, in consultation with the OECD, GPAI and other stakeholders, to introduce monitoring tools and mechanisms to help organizations stay accountable for the implementation of these actions.

object.value: Provides voluntary guidance for organisations developing the most advanced AI systems, including the most advanced foundation models and generative AI systems ('advanced AI systems').

claims.statement: The Hiroshima Process Code of Conduct states that it will provide voluntary guidance for actions by organisations developing the most advanced AI systems, which it defines to include the most advanced foundation models and generative AI systems.

time.note: Undated PDF; date of the Leaders' Statement.

claims.qualification: Defines the code's addressees by description only; it sets no compute or capability threshold.

evidence.passage: will provide voluntary guidance for actions by organizations developing the most advanced AI systems, including the most advanced foundation models and generative AI systems (henceforth "advanced AI systems").

claims.subject: g7-hiroshima-code-of-conduct-2023

object.value: Action 1: identify, evaluate and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle, including diverse internal and independent external testing such as red-teaming.

claims.statement: Action 1 of the Hiroshima Process Code of Conduct calls for appropriate measures throughout development, including before and during deployment, to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks, including diverse internal and independent external testing such as red-teaming.
